name: Sonnit
tagline: An AI writing tool that turns prompts and rough notes into finished drafts.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: Public detail on Sonnit is thin, so treat this as a category call rather than a forensic teardown. Products in this shape are a text editor, a library of prompt templates, and a streaming call to a model somebody else trained. None of those three pieces are hard, and the only one with real cost is the model, which you rent by the token with your own API key. A coding agent can put a local version in front of you in an afternoon, and you will likely pay less than a subscription unless you generate enormous volume. The honest caveat: if Sonnit turns out to be doing something structural like a fine-tuned house model or a deep CMS integration layer, downgrade this to kinda.
coreLoopDIY: A local writing workspace where you pick a prompt template, feed it notes, stream a draft from your own model API key, and keep versions in a SQLite file.
requirements: An API key for an LLM provider (OpenAI or Anthropic)
Node 20 and a willingness to run a local dev server
Per-token model spend, which is usually cents per draft
whatYouLose: Polished editor behavior: slash commands, inline rewrites, keyboard muscle memory that someone spent a year sanding down
Prompt templates that were tested against thousands of real users instead of your three guesses
Mobile and tablet access, unless you also host it somewhere
Anything team shaped: shared drafts, comments, brand voice profiles
Someone else eating provider outages, model deprecations, and rate limits
moatNotes: The model is rented, not owned, so the defensible part is the interface and the prompt craft on top of it.
whyPeopleStillPay: Because a writing tool lives or dies on feel, and feel is exactly what a one-shot build gets wrong first. Paid tools ship a tuned set of prompts, a fast editor, and a mobile surface, so writing happens when the idea shows up instead of when you are at your laptop with a dev server running. If you write for a living, that friction is worth more than the subscription. If you write occasionally and mostly want an LLM with your own house style baked in, the local build wins on price and privacy.
notes: Category verdict, not a product autopsy: public information here is sparse, so weigh the reasoning over the label.
prompt:
Build a local AI writing workspace called Scribe. Single user, runs on my machine, no accounts, no telemetry, no cloud database.

Stack, non negotiable:
- Next.js with the App Router and TypeScript
- Tailwind for styling, no component library
- SQLite via better-sqlite3, file at ./data/scribe.db, schema created on first boot
- Anthropic and OpenAI SDKs, key read from .env.local (ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, OPENAI_API_KEY), never committed, never sent anywhere else

Features in scope:
1. Document list: create, rename, delete, search by title. Stored in SQLite.
2. Editor: plain markdown textarea with live preview toggle. Autosave on a 1 second debounce.
3. Prompt templates: seed the database with 8 templates (blog post from notes, tighten this, rewrite in plain English, expand outline, counterargument pass, email from bullets, headline options, summarize). Templates are editable rows with a name and a body containing a {{input}} placeholder and an optional {{style}} placeholder.
4. Generate: pick a template, pick selected text or the whole document as input, stream the response token by token into a right hand panel. Buttons to insert at cursor, replace selection, or discard.
5. Style profile: one editable text blob describing my voice, injected as {{style}} and as a system prompt prefix. Single row in the database.
6. Versions: every accepted insertion snapshots the previous document body. Version list with diff view and one click restore.
7. Model picker in the header: a small hardcoded list of current Anthropic and OpenAI chat models, plus a temperature slider. Persist the last choice.
8. Export: download any document as .md, and a Dump All button that writes every document to ./exports as markdown files.

Out of scope, do not build: auth, multi user, comments, billing, SEO tooling, publishing integrations, a mobile app, Docker.

Deliver a README with setup in under six commands, a .env.example, and a seed script. Handle missing API keys and provider errors with a visible inline message rather than a crash.
